text: Provides a REST interface to MCP servers, handling protocol, OAuth and credential management for you
quote: Smithery gives you a simple REST interface for connecting to MCP servers. Instead of implementing the MCP protocol directly, handling OAuth flows, and managing credentials yourself, Smithery handles all of it for you.

text: Automatically refreshes OAuth tokens so credentials stay valid without manual work
quote: Automatic token refresh — Credentials stay valid without manual intervention

text: Stores API keys and tokens in encrypted, write-only credential storage
quote: Secure credential storage — Encrypted, write-only storage for API keys and tokens

text: Uplink bridges a locally running MCP server into a managed remote Smithery connection without deploying it
quote: Uplink exposes an MCP server running on any machine as a regular Smithery connection.

text: Lets developers test an in-progress MCP server against a real agent before publishing it
quote: You’re developing an MCP server and want to test it against a real agent before publishing.

text: Service tokens let you expose Smithery safely to browsers, mobile apps and AI agents without leaking the main API key
quote: Service tokens let you safely expose Smithery to browsers, mobile apps, and AI agents without leaking your API key.

text: Scoped tokens can be restricted to only list/call tools for a specific end-user's connections
quote: This token can list and call tools on connections in `my-app` where `metadata.userId` is `user-123` — nothing else.

text: Deep links let supported clients auto-configure an MCP connection when a user clicks the link
quote: Deep links provide a seamless way to integrate Smithery MCPs into supported clients. When a user clicks a deep link from our server page, the client automatically configures the MCP with the correct settings.

text: Servers already deployed elsewhere can be published on Smithery via a simple URL registration method
quote: If you’ve already deployed an MCP server elsewhere, you can publish it directly on Smithery via the URL method.

text: Local stdio servers are distributed as a pre-built MCPB bundle that clients download and run locally
quote: For local stdio servers — Smithery distributes a pre-built MCPB bundle that clients download and run locally.

text: Servers that can't be auto-scanned can supply metadata manually via a static server-card.json file
quote: If automatic scanning can’t complete (auth wall, required configuration, or other issues), you can provide server metadata manually via a static server card at `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`

text: Triggers let a server surface upstream events, with Smithery proxying subscribe calls through to the server
quote: Triggers let an MCP server surface events from its upstream service. When a consumer activates a trigger via Smithery, Smithery proxies the subscribe call straight through to your server

text: Aggregates connections to multiple MCP servers so an agent can use all their tools together
quote: Connect to multiple servers and aggregate their tools

text: Namespaces act as shared workspaces so a team can manage resources under one scoped API key
quote: Namespaces act as a shared workspace. Resources within a namespace can be managed by anyone with the appropriate API key scoped to that namespace, making them suitable for team collaboration similar to project IDs.

text: Generates a typed TypeScript SDK automatically from each published server's tool and trigger schemas
quote: Every MCP server published on Smithery gets a typed TypeScript SDK generated from its tool and trigger schemas.

text: Official CLI can search the registry and add MCP server connections
quote:
smithery mcp search [term]              # Search the Smithery registry
smithery mcp add <url>                  # Add an MCP server connection

text: Official CLI can search for tools by name/intent and call a tool on a connection
quote:
smithery tool find [query]             # Search tools by name or intent
smithery tool call <connection> <tool> [args]  # Call a tool

text: Provides a Skills Registry where users can browse and install skills via an upstream installer
quote: Browse skills on the [Smithery Skills Registry](https://smithery.ai/skills) and install them with the upstream installer

text: Catalog includes deep third-party integrations like Exa, Context7 and Browserbase for web search, docs and browser control
quote: Exa - Search the live web, access LinkedIn profiles, do deep research, and more

text: Supports running a private tool for yourself or your team without needing to host it separately
quote: You want to run a private tool for yourself or your team without hosting it.
